searchText: port I can see value in for local testing, but no relay/builder today has a port in their url and it's not gonna be relevant for mainnet a builder saying they explicitly want a trailing slash to be signed over sounds absurd to me they can use custom auth data for that but even port isn't relevant for local testing if you use kurtosis seems like prysm, lighthouse, lodestar are fine (based on back references), <@641548687813902336> is teku ok with this? I guess <@808969530608451584> any concern signing over hostname vs. host vs. raw url? yeah, just need to fix it, we add trailing slash for the calls but still sign whatever raw string url is configured, but just hostname would make it consistent across, would make the change yeah should decide on this rather sooner than later, once we are on testnet it will cause more issues, but right now there are 2 builders which is bombora and buildoor yeah, let's agree on hostname just one thing, why not UTF-8 bytes instead of ASCII to be consistent with the beacon API it barely makes a difference but any standardized hostname is ascii, eg. `new URL(<url>).hostname` in browsers, and there are several rfc on this that state ascii should be used https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/642 does this resolve the beacon-api concern? should make sure we don't state that it's utf-8 anywhere else I was thinking about https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/ef98d512c03c8ca6b9d7cbdc45b9293ec2b24722/types/gloas/builder_entry.yaml#L22 but that is a raw url to send the http request using utf-8 to convert raw string to bytes for ssz seems to be common pattern - gossip topics: "plain UTF-8 strings" - protocol IDs in req/resp: "case-sensitive UTF-8 string" - the req/resp error_message, a List[byte, 256]: "MAY be interpreted as a UTF-8 string" Yeah, let's leave the auth data as ascii actually I agree, doesn't cause any issues either way and is more precise yeah not sure how it works in java, but any standard library that has a `hostname` (per rfc) will produce ascii output per https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-url-hostname I mean for the germans, `new URL("https://bücher.example/").hostname` would be `xn--bcher-kva.example`, kinda strange but that's the spec seems bit mixed, but as you said, I don't think this makes a pratical difference also per https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc5890/ domain names need to be ascii, ie. use punycode otherwise if not compliant I think it's fine as is, leaving final approval to <@808969530608451584> since he is the biggest builder by far I think that's the right format we should use on the wire. clients/builders can still decide to parse punycode to it. but it's a rarely used feature anyway. we can probably set up a builder behind a https://xn--platberget-45a.dev/ url 😄 wtf, if I try to copy the url here, on linux, it auto converts it to `https://xn--platberget-45a.dev/` discord converts it to ascii 😄 browser renders it properly so you are saying `https://xn--platberget-45a.dev/` should be set as url or the weird other character? ah that was not a reply, wanted to mention that I'll gonna merge it 😄 nah it's my system, not only discord platåberget works as soon as i make it a url, my system converts it the ascii format should be the auth data that's signed over xn-- version 😉 not the platå.. version well the other one is impossible on my system anyways `https://platåberget.dev` manually constructing it works 😄 ah I see, so if you copy pase it from brave, it does that lodestar already on current trunk branch doesn't accept such a url its a display feature 😄 technically that xn-- version is the domain name. So yea, when parsing the flag you might support the punnycode version too, but that fully optional imo yeah so `new URL("https://platåberget.dev").hostname` = `xn--platberget-45a.dev` that seems right to me so <@808969530608451584> we are good with https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/168, I also merged the lodestar pr btw in case you wanna e2e in ci yes, looks good 🙂 https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10127 best I can offer for users 😄
